I read the structure region by region and assembled the SMILES from these parts.

**Biphenyl part (left, top).** The first ring carries F and CO2H on adjacent carbons. Ring atoms run C1 (attached to the second ring), C2 (CH), C3 (C–CO2H), C4 (C–F), C5 (CH), C6 (CH). So the CO2H carbon is ortho to F, and the aryl attachment is para to F and meta to CO2H.

**Second ring.** It is attached to the first ring at one carbon. The adjacent carbon bears OH. The next carbon bears the NH–N= group. The remaining three carbons are CH.

**Hydrazone and isatin part.** The hydrazone NH–N= links to C3 of the indolin-2-one. C2 is C=O, and N1 carries a 3,5-dimethylphenyl group. On the indole benzo ring, the CO2Me sits at C6. Going around the ring: C3a, C4 (CH), C5 (CH), C6 (CO2Me), C7 (CH), C7a (attached to N). In the drawing, C3a is at the upper left of the benzo ring, and CO2Me is on the lower right carbon, which is adjacent to the C7 carbon next to C7a. This matches C6.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond has drawn geometry. At the top of the hydrazone, N (=N) sits above C3. The NH is up-left of the =N, and the C2 carbonyl is on the left of C3. The N–NH substituent and C2 look to be on the same side (Z).

I write it as C3(=N/NHAr) with C2 on the same side. The SMILES fragment is O=C1N(Ar)c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2/C1=N\Nc..., and I need to check the geometry of that form.

For `C1=N\N`, the bond written before C1 is `/C1` from the aromatic carbon c2. The atom c2 precedes C1 with a `/` bond: `c2/C1=N\N`. This means c2 is "below" C1 and N–N is "below" N, so c2 and NH are on the same side. Therefore C2 (the carbonyl, ring closure 1) is on the opposite side to NH, which gives E. I want C2 and NH on the same side, so I use `c2/C1=N/N`, which puts NH on the opposite side of c2 and hence on the same side as C2. This gives Z.

**Final SMILES.**
O=C1N(c3cc(C)cc(C)c3)c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2/C1=N/Nc4cccc(c4O)-c5ccc(F)c(C(=O)O)c5
